france24fr.title: Cisjordanie occupée : à Masafer Yatta, des colons israéliens installés en zone militaire interdite
france24fr.description: Dans la région de Masafer Yatta en Cisjordanie occupée, des colons israéliens ont installé au moins neuf avant-postes illégaux au cours des années 2020. La zone est pourtant officiellement considérée depuis 2022 comme une aire militaire par Israël, qui y interdit toute construction. En septembre, l’armée israélienne y a démoli trois villages palestiniens, considérés comme des "structures illégales".

france24fr.title: Désinformation : la Russie multiplie les faux reportages
france24fr.description:
📈 Le nombre d’opérations d'influence russes 🇷🇺 visant à imiter des médias pour diffuser de fausses informations a augmenté de 850 % entre le 1er semestre 2025 et le 1er semestre 2026, selon un rapport publié lundi 28 septembre par l’observatoire de la désinformation Newsguard. ➡️ Décryptage. 
 
🔗 Cette vidéo a été réalisée dans le cadre du projet CLIC, qui lutte contre la propagation de contenus trompeurs. Rendez-vous sur le site clicproject.org pour en savoir plus.

france24fr.title: France : les étudiants rejoignent la contestation des lycéens, une cellule de crise convoquée
france24fr.description: Alors que les blocages de lycées continuent jeudi à travers la France, notamment en région parisienne, à Marseille, Strasbourg, ou encore Rennes, des facultés ont rejoint le mouvement. Une trentaine de campus sont concernés à Paris, Strasbourg, Marseille, Lyon 2, Reims, Poitiers ou encore Nanterre, selon l'Union étudiante.

france24fr.title: "Super héros du ciel" : qui est Smit Machchhar, ce pilote qui a évité le pire sur le vol Flydubai ?
france24fr.description: Commandant de bord du vol Flydubai, le pilote indien Smit Machchhar a permis mercredi de sauver les 174 passagers à bord du vol FZ 1073 en actionnant l'ouverture de la porte du cockpit alors qu'il venait d'être poignardé par son copilote. Son héroïsme est salué partout dans le monde.

france24fr.title: Budget 2027 : le gouvernement face à l’équation des 54 milliards
france24fr.description: Dernier budget de l'ère Macron, le projet de loi de finances et celui de financement de la Sécurité sociale s’ouvrent dans un contexte tendu : déficit en hausse, dette record et absence de majorité à l’Assemblée. Le gouvernement vise 5 % de déficit en 2027, au prix de 54 milliards d’euros d’efforts.

france24fr.title: Le gouvernement lève le voile sur son budget 2027, sous la pression des marchés
france24fr.description: Le gouvernement dévoile jeudi son projet de budget pour 2027, affichant sa volonté de "redresser" les finances publiques du pays avec notamment des mesures sur les retraites, au moment où les taux d'intérêt de la dette française flambent.

france24fr.title: Etats-Unis : Hegseth dit avoir réduit de 20% le nombre de généraux dans l'armée
france24fr.description: Le ministre de la Défense américain Pete Hegseth a affirmé mercredi avoir réduit de 20% le nombre de généraux et amiraux dans l'armée, dans un discours depuis une base militaire en Virginie (est).

france24fr.title: Blocus des lycées : la mobilisation continue, appel à un "acte deux" jeudi
france24fr.description: La mobilisation des lycéens s'est poursuivie mercredi, émaillée par des violences que le président Macron a condamnées, l'Union syndicale lycéenne appelant à une convergence des luttes avec les étudiants et à un "acte deux" jeudi.

france24fr.title: Les Libanais souhaitent "que nous restions sur le terrain", affirme le chef des Casques bleus
france24fr.description: Dans un entretien accordé à France 24, le chef des Casques bleus, Jean-Pierre Lacroix, assure que les Libanais souhaitent "que nous restions sur le terrain" après la fin de la Finul, prévue le 31 décembre. Il reconnaît qu'après des coupes budgétaires de 25 % dues aux impayés américains, l'ONU est "moins en mesure" de protéger les populations.

france24fr.title: 10 ans du Brexit : un retour du Royaume-Uni dans l'UE envisagé par Burnham
france24fr.description: Le Premier ministre travailliste Andy Burnham a relancé mercredi l'idée d'un retour possible du Royaume-Uni dans l'Union européenne, une première pour un chef du gouvernement britannique depuis le Brexit.

france24fr.title: Football : Cristiano Ronaldo claque la porte de la Seleçao après un clash
france24fr.description: Cristiano Ronaldo a confirmé le clash avec le nouveau sélectionneur Jorge Jesus et provoqué un psychodrame au Portugal en quittant mercredi le rassemblement de la Seleçao à Copenhague, à la veille d'un match de Ligue des nations contre le Danemark.

spiegel.description: Wenn Gallensteine auf Wanderschaft gehen, kann es zu starken Schmerzen kommen. Wie sie entstehen, welche Ernährung hilft – und was Frauen bei der Pille beachten sollten.

spiegel.title: US-Anleihen: Renditen steigen auf höchsten Stand seit fast 25 Jahren

spiegel.description: Ein vier Jahre altes Mädchen starb nach einer Vollnarkose in einer Zahnarztpraxis. Das Landgericht Frankfurt am Main hat den zuständigen Anästhesisten nun in einem erneuten Prozess wegen Mordes für schuldig befunden.

spiegel.description: Nach der Geburt ihrer Tochter litt Ashley Tisdale an einer Depression. Nun berichtet sie, wie das ihre Ehe belastet hat – im Podcast ihres Ehemanns.

letemps.title: A New York, Zohran Mamdani perd une manche contre les riches propriétaires
letemps.description:
Projet phare du maire de New York, la taxation des résidences secondaires de luxe a été balayée par un tribunal ce mardi. Le démocrate socialiste doit revoir sa copie, cependant il ne sort pas forcément perdant

Zohran Mamdani le présentait comme l’une de ses plus grandes réussites: l’instauration d’un nouvel impôt sur les résidences secondaires dont la valeur dépasse 5 millions de dollar

letemps.title: Dette de la France: tous les tabous seront visés
letemps.description:
CHRONIQUE. A quoi ressemblerait une crise de la dette de la France? Pour éviter un éclatement de la zone euro, les pays membres de l’UE seraient bien forcés de sortir de leur zone de confort. Tout se jouera sur les conditions. A ce jeu, la défense face à la menace russe pourrait servir de monnaie d’échange, écrit l’économiste Charles Wyplosz

Aujourd’hui, la dette est de 120% du PIB et les tau

letemps.title: Au salon du frontalier suisse, une disparition inquiétante
letemps.description: HEIDI.NEWS. Le Salon du frontalier est organisé tous les ans par le lobby des travailleurs français en Suisse. On s’y masse avec des CV immaculés et des yeux qui brillent, en quête de bons tuyaux. Mais il manque quelque chose...

letemps.title: Israël: la condamnation doit être religieuse
letemps.description:
CHRONIQUE. Il n'est pas question d'attendre de toute personne juive de se positionner sur la situation au Moyen-Orient, en revanche leurs chefs spirituels dont la religion est instrumentalisée doivent déconstruire ce discours de «critique impossible d'Israël», écrit Anne-Sylvie Sprenger

La question est lancinante – dans les médias, dans les esprits. «A-t-on le droit de critiquer I

letemps.title: En direct, guerre en Ukraine – Un drone russe a frappé un site de recherche nucléaire à Kiev
letemps.description:
La Russie a mené une attaque massive mercredi sur la capitale ukrainienne, visant notamment les réseaux électriques. A la chambre basse du parlement russe, les vétérans d’Ukraine occupent 10% des sièges. Notre suivi

observador.title: EUA. Dois mortos e um desaparecido após queda de helicóptero
observador.description: Helicóptero, com cinco pessoas a bordo, caiu ao mar depois de descolar da ilha de Catalina. Buscas pelo desaparecido prolongaram-se durante a noite. Acidente vai ser investigado pelas autoridades.

observador.title: Corpo de mulher encontrado em praia em Viana do Castelo
observador.description: A mulher era residente em Viana do Castelo e a PJ de Braga está já a investigar as causas da morte. O alerta foi dado esta sexta-feira pelas 7h12.

observador.title: Protestos sociais. Faculdades unem-se a escolas secundárias
observador.description: O movimento iniciado há uma semana nos subúrbios da capital ganhou escala nacional: escolas e faculdades encerradas de Paris a Marselha. Estudantes exigem substituição de professores e mais recursos.

observador.title: Assembleia da Lourinhã solidária com contestação a mina
observador.description: Promovido pela empresa Motamineral, o projeto destina-se à exploração de areias cauliníticas e massas minerais de argila, numa área de 107,7 hectares, com três núcleos de exploração a céu aberto.

observador.title: Governo reserva 3,8 milhões para "Botija de Gás Solidária"
observador.description: Medida "Botija de Gás Solidária" começou por ser de 10 euros por unidade, tendo depois subido para 15 euros e, posteriormente, para 25 euros por garrafa.

observador.title: Rita Azevedo Gomes estreia "Fuck the Polis"
observador.description: Filme distinguido com o grande prémio do Festival de Cinema de Marselha, que surge de uma viagem às ilhas gregas, está em exibição nas cidades de Coimbra, Lisboa, Leiria, Porto e Setúbal.

observador.title: Seguro quer políticas públicas de acesso à água potável
observador.description: Chefe de Estado afirma que "Portugal tem a felicidade de ter recursos hídricos naturais preciosos, mas também a responsabilidade de cuidar deles adequadamente".

observador.title: Depressão Hanna perde intensidade mas deve afetar Açores
observador.description: Apesar de estar enfraquecida, a depressão vai condicionar o tempo em todas as ilhas. Os avisos amarelos para precipitação mantêm-se. No grupo Oriental a depressão prolonga-se até sábado de manhã.

observador.title: IL propõe serviços mínimos obrigatórios na educação
observador.description: Liberais querem alterar as obrigações de prestação de serviços mínimos durante as greves, para assegurar o funcionamento durante o período letivo e não "prejudicar o percurso escolar dos alunos".

observador.title: Fabian Figueiredo volta ao Parlamento após um mês
observador.description: Numa publicação na rede social Facebook, Fabian Figueiredo escreve que retoma esta quinta-feira o mandato após uma pausa motivada por "motivos pessoais".

observador.title: Agricultores convocam marcha lenta contra subida dos custos
observador.description: Protesto será na sexta-feira, com concentrações em Serpa, às 7h00, e Vila Nova de São Bento, no mesmo concelho do distrito de Beja, às 7h30. São esperados "cerca de 80 tratores e viaturas".

observador.title: As notícias das 14h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: 62 docentes afastados por antecendentes criminais
observador.description: Professores apresentavam antecedentes de crimes como abuso sexual de menores, pornografia infantil e violência doméstica. O Ministério da Educação revelou afastamento provisório esta quarta-feira.

observador.title: Livre diz que "era evidente que Chega ia apoiar" Governo
observador.description: Porta-voz do Livre considerou que, na quarta-feira, "as direitas uniram-se uma vez mais para facilitar despejos, para dificultar ainda mais o acesso à habitação".

observador.title: Custo de vida. PCP diz que Governo respondeu com "chantagem"
observador.description: Líder da bancada comunista criticou o Governo por falar de estabilidade política, enquanto, considerou, as suas "opções políticas só estão a gerar instabilidade".

observador.title: Banco de Portugal alerta para nova fraude com cartões
observador.description: Banco de Portugal alerta que o processo para ativação de um novo cartão é "um processo atempado" e que não exige urgência. E recomenda não utilizar os links ou QR codes indicados em cartas.

observador.title: IGAS. 224 processos por assédio e uma sanção disciplinar
observador.description: O novo relatório da Inspeção-Geral das Atividades em Saúde revela que foram 224 processos relacionados a alegações de assédio, sendo mais de 150 em hospitais do SNS, a maioria por assédio moral.

observador.title: Carlos Cabreiro diz ter condições para dirigir PJ
observador.description: Remetendo para “sede própria” todas as respostas às suspeitas que pendem sobre si, Carlos Cabreiro disse ainda sentir ter a confiança do Ministério da Justiça, que tutela a Polícia Judiciária.

nyt.title: How a Cornell Student Went From Shame to Seeking Justice
nyt.description: The woman known as “Jane Doe” was initially embarrassed about what happened at a fraternity party in 2024, but soon concluded: “I was assaulted.”

nyt.title: The Cornell Rape Investigation: Five Takeaways
nyt.description: The New York Times obtained more than 1,000 pages from the university’s internal inquiry into accusations by “Jane Doe.” Here are the revelations so far.

nyt.title: Statement Written by Police in Cornell Assault Case Omitted Her Claim She Was Raped
nyt.description: Documents obtained by The New York Times show that the campus police at Cornell University sent a condensed statement to a prosecutor, who then declined to bring charges.

nyt.title: What Newly Obtained Documents Show About the Cornell Case, and Inside the Bloody Midair Cockpit Attack
nyt.description: Plus, a Kelvin wave is coming.

nyt.title: After Failed Attempt to Execute Christa Pike, Tennessee Pauses a Planned Execution
nyt.description: Gov. Bill Lee, a Republican, ordered a review of the state’s lethal injection process after the botched attempt to put Christa Pike to death. She was hospitalized Wednesday.

nyt.title: What to Know About the Attempted Execution of Christa Pike
nyt.description: Ms. Pike, 50, survived two doses of lethal injection in Tennessee. She was sentenced to death for the 1995 murder of a classmate.

nyt.title: Texas Governor Race Puts Pressure on Andy Beshear and Democratic Governors Association
nyt.description: Allies of Gina Hinojosa want a Democratic group to support her bid for Texas governor — putting pressure on its chairman, Gov. Andy Beshear of Kentucky, who is weighing a run for president.

nyt.title: 5 Takeaways From the Debate for California Governor
nyt.description: Xavier Becerra, a Democrat, and Steve Hilton, a Republican, sparred over President Trump, taxes and immigration in their only scheduled meeting.

nyt.title: Who Is Captain Smit Machchhar, the Pilot Hailed as a Hero After FlyDubai Cockpit Stabbing?
nyt.description: Capt. Smit Machchhar from India suffered stab wounds while fending off an attack from his co-pilot, saving the lives of around 170 people on board, officials said.

nyt.title: A Bloody Attack on a FlyDubai Plane Headed to Israel, and a Terrifying Plunge
nyt.description: “I don’t deserve to die like this,” said one passenger on Flight 1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv. The motive of the cockpit stabbing remains unknown, officials said.

nyt.title: John Roberts Retreated to His Island. Supreme Court Critics Found Him.
nyt.description: After decades of potlucks and paddle-boarding on Maine’s midcoast, rising anger and protests have left the Supreme Court’s chief justice more isolated than ever.

nyt.title: U.S. Bond Yields Hit Highest Level Since 2002
nyt.description: The factors pushing up yields, including the war in Iran and high government debt levels, are unlikely to dissipate soon.

nyt.title: Oil Is Flowing From the Persian Gulf, but Prices Remain High. Why?
nyt.description: Crude oil costs close to $100 a barrel because traders are worried hostilities could soon restart and the world is burning through its emergency stockpiles.

nyt.title: A Way Out of the A.I. Arms Race?
nyt.description: New research points to how the world could stop short of the brink of disaster. Even with the agreement signed at the White House by tech leaders, it won’t be easy.

nyt.title: When Data Centers Cluster Together, How Dirty Are They? One County Wants Answers.
nyt.description: An unusual study aims to estimate the pollution and health costs from a cluster of proposed data centers, instead of considering each one separately.

nyt.title: A Hacking Competition Shows the Power of China’s ‘Open Weight’ A.I.
nyt.description: The winner of an elite cybersecurity contest prevailed by relying on a free Chinese model — another sign that available A.I. systems could already be too powerful to easily regulate.

nyt.title: New York Times Reporting Through a Front Page That Never Published and More
nyt.description: Times reporters and editors discuss items that have shaped our coverage, including Dean Baquet on the “Madam President” front page that never was.

nyt.title: Here’s Why The Times’s First Crossword Is Nearly Impossible to Solve Today
nyt.description: Even Will Shortz has no trouble admitting that it’s a doozy.

republika.title: Flydubai: chi può aprire la porta della cabina di pilotaggio e perché solo in un caso è impossibile
republika.description: Chi guida l’aereo è protetto da una barriera quasi inviolabile. Il comandante deve sempre autorizzare l’ingresso all’assistente di volo. Ma se tutti i piloti svengono o sono impossibilitati a governare il mezzo, scatta una procedura di emergenza per sbloccare l’ingresso. Procedura che non funziona nello scenario della tragedia Germanwings del 2015

republika.title: Roberto Vannacci: The General Who Flirts With Putin’s Russia — and Could Cost Meloni the Election
republika.description: In just three years, the former special forces commander who has no qualms about echoing Mussolini has gone from obscurity to the European Parliament and the leadership of a new far-right party. Behind his rise is a network of figures with ties to Moscow — and a political agenda with striking similarities to the Kremlin’s

npr.title: Passengers recount chaos on Tel Aviv flight. And, FBI probes employee-data hack
npr.description: What we know so far about the tense moments aboard a Tel Aviv-bound flight. And, the FBI investigates a cyberattack involving sensitive employee data.

npr.title: Picanha, prices and politics: What Brazil's favorite steak says about the election
npr.description: Lula promised Brazilians four years ago they'd be able to afford picanha again. Now, as he seeks another term, the price of the country's favorite cut of beef is telling a different story.

npr.title: Swiss glaciers suffer another year of record ice loss
npr.description: Switzerland's glaciers are disappearing at a record pace. More than 5% of their ice has vanished this year alone — threatening water supplies, ecosystems and communities across Europe.

npr.title: Greetings from Syria, where time seems to melt as a glassmaker braves scorching temps
npr.description: As a Syrian glassmaker created his wares in Damascus, watching his craft reminded this reporter to slow down and enjoy the moment.

npr.title: How Ukrainians are coping with new, more deadly Russian attacks
npr.description: Zanny Minton Beddoes, The Economist's editor in chief, just visited Ukraine. She says, despite all its drone weaponry, Kyiv is under extraordinary bombardment, as Russia tries to make it unlivable.

npr.title: A midair stabbing on a flight to Israel is being investigated as a possible terrorist attack
npr.description: flydubai airline said the motives behind the incident were unknown and remain subject to a formal investigation. Israel's Prime Minister Netanyahu described it as "a serious security incident."

npr.title: U.S. forces exit Iraq amid Iran war. And, SCOTUS revives Trump deportation policy

npr.title: The U.S. military withdraws from Iraq over 2 decades after its invasion
npr.description: 23 years after the United States military invaded Iraq, sparking an insurgency and a civil war, the U.S. has withdrawn its forces, as the country still tries to combat Iranian influence.

npr.title: Retired general who led troops in Iraq warns U.S. exit may give Iran, ISIS an opening
npr.description: Retired Lt. Gen. H.R. McMaster, who commanded U.S. troops in Iraq, says the withdrawal could strengthen Iran and leave Iraq more vulnerable to ISIS.

undark.description: Welcome to Season 3 of Entanglements! In our first episode, we discuss neural implants and AI with Judy Illes, a professor of neurology and neuroethics at the University of British Columbia, and Joseph J. Fins, a physician scientist and medical ethicist at Weill Cornell Medicine in New York.

undark.title: Engineering Animals to Grow Human Organs — But Not Human Minds
undark.description: Chimeras, or animals with human cells and tissues, are not new, and researchers have long used them to gain insights into diseases and even as a potential source of transplantable organs. But the research brings up thorny ethical questions regarding animal rights and the moral status of chimeric creatures.

undark.title: AI-Driven Biology Is Only as Good as the Data Beneath It
undark.description: Opinion | The biotech and pharma industries are pouring billions of dollars into AI-driven drug discovery and development. But the genomic data used to train AI models are often incomplete, contain errors, or lack contextual information — a quality issue that threatens to slow the pace of biological research.

undark.title: In Italy, What Earth Can Tell Us About Extraterrestrial Life
undark.description: Photo Essay | From sampling hydrothermal vents and abandoned mines to lab experiments that replicate Mars’ atmosphere, scientists are using what we know about life on Earth to understand how it may exist on other worlds. Italy, it seems, provides particularly fertile ground for such explorations.

undark.title: The Evolving Quest to Build Life in a Lab
undark.description: Scientists are trying to create new life, whether to understand how biology first developed on Earth, or design new cells from scratch.  But life hasn’t happened — at least not yet. And questions around safety, as well as what even constitutes life in the first place, continue to swirl.

undark.title: The Embryos That Don’t Come From Eggs and Sperm
undark.description: Human embryo models mimic the earliest development stages; they could offer a glimpse of the first weeks of pregnancy — a mysterious period for which natural embryos are seldom available — and potentially shed light on miscarriage, congenital anomalies, and other health issues. But how far should they go?

undark.title: Book Review: A Contrarian View of How Consciousness Evolved
undark.description: In “Natural Intelligence & the Logic of Consciousness,” neuroscientist Antonio Damasio argues against the conventional theory that consciousness stems from high-level brain function and cognition, which in turn leads to feelings. Instead, he writes, our basest feelings led us to our loftiest thoughts.

undark.title: AI Presents Science with a ‘Ship of Theseus’ Problem
undark.description: Opinion | AI is being integrated into every part of the scientific process, including education, publishing, and the research itself. What does it mean if every component of the enterprise gets replaced by AI tools over time? C. Brandon Ogbunu explores what happens when science gets stripped of human involvement.

undark.title: Interview: What Does the ‘I’ in AI Really Mean?
undark.description: Is it possible that AI is — or might one day become — truly intelligent? Undark posed the question to five experts in linguistics, computer science, cognitive science, and psychology. They offered very different answers, though they agreed that the term “intelligence” is vague and poorly suited to the debate.

undark.title: Book Excerpt: Why the Brain Isn’t the Self
undark.description: The brain isn’t the self — consciousness is intimately linked with the human body. And if consciousness is the body’s way of knowing itself, then it is the living form in its entirety that should be taken as selfhood proper, with the brain as an especially feverish region.

proj-syn.title: The Hard Road to a Middle-Power Order
proj-syn.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has challenged the world’s middle powers to build a better international order. Yet they are increasingly turning to coalitions of the willing and a patchwork of separate initiatives that risk entrenching zero-sum mindsets and making collective action harder.

proj-syn.title: The Sovereign Wealth Fund America Needs
proj-syn.description: Two recent proposals to establish a new US sovereign wealth fund would fail to make good on a good idea, because neither plan would produce a fund nearly large enough to meet America’s mounting financing needs. But a different approach, funded by Treasury sales, could.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Vanity Summit With Xi
proj-syn.description: While expectations for the summit between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping were low, it was disappointing to watch them prioritize pageantry over substance. Trump’s cringe-worthy declarations of heartfelt admiration for Xi reflect his twisted sense that the trappings of power are power itself.

proj-syn.title: Human Rights and Populist Wrongs
proj-syn.description: For the first time, all the UK’s political parties on the right favor withdrawing from the European Convention on Human Rights. But the story of the Hillsborough Law shows how human-rights laws, not least the ECHR, help ordinary people hold the state accountable for its costliest failings.

proj-syn.title: Is Another Eurozone Debt Crisis Looming?
proj-syn.description: At a time when the cost of servicing sovereign debt is rising globally, France stands out as an especially fragile case. Its public debt-to-GDP ratio is edging up toward that of Greece on the eve of its sovereign-debt crisis, and the French political system seems unable to do anything about it.

proj-syn.title: Will AI Reverse the Renminbi’s Rise?
proj-syn.description: In China, AI-driven productivity gains will most likely be in non-tradable services, which could push down relative prices and put downward pressure on the renminbi’s real exchange rate. To ensure that this does not also mean lower income and weaker demand, policymakers should ensure that the productivity dividend is broadly shared.

proj-syn.title: The Price of You
proj-syn.description: As more people shop online, firms are increasingly setting individualized prices based on personal data, including purchase history, location, demographics, behavior, and biometric data. AI threatens to turbocharge such surveillance pricing, further widening the gap between privacy expectations and reality.

proj-syn.title: Investing in Brain Health
proj-syn.description: Just as AI agents are mastering complex cognitive tasks, our own ability to perform the same tasks is eroding. Whether AI vindicates its boosters or fizzles out like the Metaverse craze of 2022, we will not fare well without a civilization-wide effort to rebuild the cognitive skills that make technological progress possible.

proj-syn.title: Europe Still Needs Molecules
proj-syn.description: Not even the most effective European electrification strategy will eliminate the need for the molecules that fossil fuels provide. Given this, Europe must diversify its oil and gas supplies, maintain its refining capacity, and lock in decarbonization by building a hydrogen-energy industry at scale.

proj-syn.title: Energy Security in an Age of Disruption
proj-syn.description: While there is no single prescription for energy security, strengthening “response capacity,” such as by establishing stockpiles, substituting sources, and diversifying suppliers, is essential. The point is not to eliminate vulnerabilities altogether, but to ensure that there are options when disruption arrives.

proj-syn.title: Africa’s Common Currency-in-Waiting
proj-syn.description: While the phased approach of the Economic Community of West African States to implementing a long-delayed single currency will maintain momentum without compromising macroeconomic discipline, the bloc still lacks a robust mechanism to address asymmetric shocks. That is why fiscal integration must come first.

proj-syn.title: Learning to Reconcile
proj-syn.description: Political discourse in many Western countries has broken down, making it difficult for people with different viewpoints to live amicably with one another. The Reconciliation League, an international initiative by 13 universities and colleges, aims to train a generation of leaders who can change that.

proj-syn.title: Sheinbaum Is Just Another Trump Appeaser
proj-syn.description: After two years in office, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum continues to be widely praised, both in Mexico and abroad, for her handling of US President Donald Trump. But Sheinbaum has skillfully—and cynically—disguised the extent to which she has deferred to Trump on almost every issue.

proj-syn.title: Distorted Intelligence at the AI Frontier
proj-syn.description: The real problem for the frontier AI labs is not that their models are too powerful and already “misaligned” with the goals their creators set for them. Rather, it is that the models are being trained in ways that may be leading to a type of intelligence that will become less predictable.

proj-syn.title: Good Growth Requires the Right Public Finance
proj-syn.description: Although the Labour Party has done more to strengthen the United Kingdom's public-finance ecosystem in the past two years than any government in a generation, it must not stop there. If public investment is to meet its full potential, it must be reorganized to operate at scale on the public's behalf.

proj-syn.title: An EU–Canada Partnership Against Coercion

proj-syn.title: The Opposing Forces Reshaping Global Finance
proj-syn.description: The financial industry is being pulled between two powerful forces: bottom-up financial technology is enabling seamless integration, while top-down geoeconomic statecraft is promoting fragmentation. So much for the conventional wisdom that finance will simply become smoother, cheaper, and more globalized over time.

proj-syn.title: The Dismally Obedient Science
proj-syn.description: While empirical inquiry has its place in economics, the pursuit of causality must not be allowed to displace the pursuit of explanation. Beyond identifying causal effects within existing arrangements, economists must investigate how those arrangements are produced, reproduced, and contested.
